## Haul-Fleet Operating Rate, Projects & Workforce Analysis

**All three areas show deterioration:** Haul-fleet operating and effective rates have dropped year-on-year, 9 capital projects are over budget (3 by >400%), and workforce readiness tracking has stopped since July 2026.

### Evidence

**Operating Rate Decline (OPS telemetry):**

| Period | Autonomy | Operating Rate | Effective Rate | Down Hours | Queue Hours |
|--------|----------|----------------|----------------|------------|-------------|
| Q2 FY2026 | Autonomous | 80.2% | 69.0% | 2,587 h | 7,171 h |
| Q2 FY2027 | Autonomous | 76.7% | 61.4% | 1,210 h | 2,344 h |
| Q2 FY2026 | Manned | 79.6% | 68.5% | 1,021 h | 2,711 h |
| Q2 FY2027 | Manned | 75.1% | 60.1% | 542 h | 869 h |

Autonomous operating rate fell 3.5 percentage points and effective rate dropped 7.6 pp; manned fleet declined 4.5 pp and 8.4 pp respectively. The pattern suggests systemic queue/standby issues reducing productivity, not downtime (which actually improved).

**Critical Over-Budget Projects (SAP):**

- **CB PPM** (R007023): 2,226% of plan; $552k vs. $24.8k budget
- **BL LNG Plattform** (ONG.PROJECT.19): 437% of plan; $13.5M vs. $3.1M
- **Integration Platforms** (R007026): 899% of plan; $475k vs. $52.8k

Additionally, 26 projects with no plan have spent $17.1M and are past their end date (SAP).

**Workforce Readiness Gap (SAP):** Readiness was stable at 95.1% through July 2026 (1,682 people), but **no status has been recorded since August 2026**—a 2.5-month data blackout.

### Chain: Signal → Risk → Action

Queue hours and standby time drive low effective rates → fewer hauled tonnes → higher unit cost. Over-budget projects drain capital; untracked workforce readiness risks safety compliance and operational continuity.

**Next Step:** Convene a 48-hour task force to (1) restore workforce-readiness reporting, (2) audit the three most over-budget projects for stop/restructure decisions, and (3) map haul-fleet queue root causes (loader availability, dispatch logic, pit access).
